## Summary

The IEEE registry lists one MA-L block, B0:09:DA, to Ring Solutions at 1200 Atwater Drive, Suite 225, Malvern, Pennsylvania, registered on 24 May 2017 [1][2]. Ring Solutions is the Malvern home-automation engineering unit of Ring: the Philadelphia Inquirer reported in February 2018 that the team came from Zonoff, a 70-employee Malvern Internet of Things home-automation firm that shut down abruptly the previous winter, that Ring named Zonoff founder Mike Harris president of its new automation unit in the Atwater business park, and that Amazon was buying Ring for about 1 billion US dollars [3]. Ring, founded in autumn 2013 as the crowdfunded startup Doorbot and headquartered in Santa Monica, became an Amazon subsidiary when Amazon completed the purchase on 12 April 2018 and launched Ring Alarm in July 2018 [4].

A MAC in this block is therefore most likely a Ring home-automation device such as an alarm base station, but no source consulted ties the block to a specific product, so found_in is empty and the radios are inferred. Ring's current Alarm Base Station lists Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Z-Wave, Zigbee, Bluetooth for setup, and cellular backup with a compatible Ring Protect subscription [5].

Ring as a whole agreed a 5.8 million US dollar FTC settlement in May 2023 after the FTC said Ring compromised customers' privacy by letting any employee or contractor access their private videos, and in December 2019 attackers took over Ring cameras and broadcast racial slurs and threats through their speakers [4]. The FCC ID databases (fccid.io, fcc.report, apps.fcc.gov) refused this session's requests, so no grantee code is listed; no teardown naming the base station silicon was reachable, and no source documents MAC randomization.
